skills.name: import-memory
skills.description: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.

skills.name: deal-review
skills.description: Pull a live deal from HubSpot and produce a structured Dexory deal review covering an exec summary, next steps, hidden risks, and deal acceleration ideas. Use this skill whenever Abby mentions reviewing a deal, checking on a pipeline opportunity, preparing for a deal call or QBR, or asks anything like "what should I do with this deal", "review this opportunity", "what are the risks on X", or "how can I accelerate Y". Trigger even if the request is brief — e.g. "review Maersk" or "what's the status on the IKEA deal". Always fetch live data from HubSpot rather than relying on memory.

skills.name: morning
skills.description: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.

skills.name: pdf
skills.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.

skills.name: morning-brief
skills.description: Send a direct Slack message to myself each morning to help me catch up: today's and upcoming meetings, important unread emails, messages needing a reply, and prioritized action items across all my projects. Use only when I ask to run or set up my morning brief, or invoke /morning-brief by name.

skills.name: briefing-sources
skills.description: Shared source-gathering logic for briefing skills — how to pull Basecamp, GitHub, Slack, email, calendar, and meeting-transcript data, over what time window, and how to check freshness before surfacing anything as outstanding. Not invoked directly by the user; called by other skills (morning brief, stand-up prep, end-of-day report) with a project scope and time window.

skills.name: gtm-intelligence
skills.description: Dexory's warehouse GTM intelligence — buyer and user personas, jobs-to-be-done, vertical positioning, buyer insights, objections, lifecycle plays, proof points and customer references. Use this skill WHENEVER producing any go-to-market or sales/marketing content for Dexory, even if the personas are not explicitly mentioned. That includes writing or reviewing outbound email and LinkedIn sequences, cold outreach, nurture and lifecycle campaigns, battlecards, discovery-call questions, call and meeting prep, demo narratives, one-pagers, landing-page or ad copy, value propositions, vertical or persona-specific messaging, objection handling, ROI and business-case framing, and competitive positioning versus manual counting and drones. Also use it for any persona research question (what an Inventory Manager cares about, who signs off, which KPIs matter) and whenever tailoring a message to a warehouse role, buying centre, vertical, or funnel stage.

skills.name: standup-prep
skills.description: Send a direct Slack message to myself summarizing everything worth mentioning at my daily stand-up for a specific project: Basecamp board movement/comments, related GitHub PR reviews, Slack activity, emails, and meeting/transcript follow-ups, since the last stand-up. Use only when I ask to run or set up my stand-up prep, or invoke /standup-prep by name.

skills.name: skill-creator
skills.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.

skills.name: business-case-advisor
skills.description: Build a grounded, credible DexoryView business case by combining a site questionnaire, live HubSpot deal data (including meeting notes and call context from meeting descriptions), the Forrester TEI study, and indicative Dexory pricing. Identifies the strongest benefit areas to focus on, flags where TEI assumptions need moderating, and surfaces knowledge gaps that must be filled before a robust ROI model can be presented. Use this skill whenever Abby or the sales team needs to scope a business case, review a questionnaire response, prioritise which benefits to lead with for a specific prospect, identify missing data, or pressure-test TEI numbers before sharing with a prospect. Trigger even for partial inputs — e.g. "we've only filled in sections 2 and 3", "build a business case for [deal name]", or "what's the most important question to ask next?" — the skill should work with whatever data exists.

skills.name: docx
skills.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.

skills.name: xlsx
skills.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.

skills.name: pptx
skills.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.

skills.name: dexory-brand
skills.description: Dexory's company-wide brand system — colours, type, logo, layouts and graphics. Use WHENEVER creating, designing, formatting, or restyling any Dexory deliverable: decks / presentations / pitch decks, case studies, business cases, ROI or TEI calculators and models, one-pagers, reports, proposals, battlecards, brochures and event collateral — customer-facing OR internal. Apply it even when the person never says 'brand', 'Dexory', colours or fonts, and even if they only describe the content ('make a deck on our Modex results', 'write up this business case', 'build an ROI calculator'). If the output is something someone will open, present, send or download (.pptx, .docx, .xlsx, PDF, or a designed HTML/interactive artifact), apply this skill so it carries Dexory's identity. It composes on top of the pptx, docx, xlsx and frontend-design skills and content skills (business-case-advisor, deal-review, gtm-intelligence). Default to using it; skip only for plain conversational answers, throwaway notes, or raw exports.
